correctness.rationale: Radial angular orthogonality diagonalizes T_x; Gamma integration gives a0=1-e^-x(1+x), aj=G_j+e^-x*x^j*(j-1-x)/j! for j>=1. Symbolic subtraction independently verifies the stated exact increment for j=0..19, and its sign has one upward step per unit interval. The strict comparison a_(k+1)<a_(k-1) closes the only nonadjacent ordering gap, yielding the stated unique rank k+1 selection; positive integer x=k produces exactly two zero adjacent gaps, with threefold degeneracy. A rank-one exchange yields two nonzero projection-difference eigenvalues +/-1; Stirling on the Poisson mass supplies uniform k^-3/2 gain. Finite checks at half-integers k=1..14 agree.

value.rationale: The physically canonical first-excited Landau level has a non-monotone mode ordering absent from the Gaussian ground state. Identifying exactly the exchanged mode, triple cutoff ties and persistent operator-level distance provides a useful precise sharpening of the known finite WH comparison, not a restatement of the integral spectrum.

final_claim: For the true first-excited Gaussian Fock/Landau disk Toeplitz operator, adjacent eigenvalue gaps are -exp(-x)*x^j*(x-j)*(x-j-1)/(j+1)!, integer x=k induces a triple tie at indices k-1,k,k+1 at rank k, and every noninteger x in (k,k+1) uniquely selects {0,...,k-1,k+1}, gaining exp(-x)*x^k*(x-k)*(k+1-x)/(k+1)!, with trace norm 2 between projectors and uniform k^-3/2 gain asymptotics.
limitations: Finite bounded computational checks do not establish a universal theorem; correctness is based on the reconstructed analytical proof.
